note: Monday 07:00 SGT weekend sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30) and ahead of the Sun-evening 27 Jul oil/futures reopen, after the Fri 24 Jul US close. Price levels are as of that close unless noted (oil/metals futures shut over the weekend; silver/crypto levels are the latest verifiable, ~Sat 25-26 Jul). The dominant regime shift over the weekend is a tentative US-Iran DE-ESCALATION — the US paused strikes for a SECOND straight day (Sat 26 Jul), Tehran also held fire and talks are developing — which should relieve the oil-driven rate-hike fear that pressured levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech and crypto last week. Offsetting it, a new AI-overcapacity scare (Meta reportedly pivoting from AI models to leasing spare compute) hammered semis Friday (Nasdaq -2.1%, SMIC -10% in Asia). Fresh items (5 of 13) are dated Fri 24-Sun 26 Jul. Every item source-verified; the MAS S-REIT leverage item remains flagged as reported-but-pending primary confirmation.

items.headline: US-Iran war: strikes paused for a SECOND straight day; tentative de-escalation as talks develop
items.summary: After nearly two weeks of consecutive nightly strikes, the US paused its bombing campaign on Iran for a second straight day (Sat 26 Jul), with operations described as 'on hold', and Tehran also paused its attacks. Trump is letting weekend talks develop, though neither side has verbally signaled a formal return to diplomacy. Since 27 June, 59 people have been killed in Iran and at least four US service members killed in Iranian strikes. Iran warned the war could still expand if US strikes resume.
items.actionable: This is the upside catalyst the rate-sensitive book was waiting on: a genuine pause eases the oil premium and the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressured levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech and crypto — net risk-relief for the largest part of the portfolio (bearish only the small energy long). Watch whether the pause holds into the 27 Jul oil reopen and the 29 Jul FOMC; a breakdown re-spikes oil/gold and hardens the Fed's hawkish tilt.

items.headline: AI-overcapacity scare hammers semis: SMIC -10% as Meta reportedly pivots from AI models to leasing spare compute
items.summary: Reports that Meta plans to shift focus from proprietary AI models toward cloud services and leasing out excess computing capacity triggered fears that AI-infrastructure investment may have peaked and overcapacity is looming. The panic spread to Asia, where semiconductor and optical-communications names bore the brunt — SMIC (0981.HK) fell ~10% and the US Nasdaq dropped ~2.1% on the AI-capex unwind. Within HK tech, the reaction diverged sharply: Alibaba (+1.8%), Xiaomi (+4.4%), JD and Meituan rose even as chips sold off.
items.actionable: A fresh, portfolio-specific headwind for the chip leg of the HK-tech core (SMIC) — but the sharp intra-sector divergence (Alibaba/Xiaomi up, chips down) argues for favoring the internet/consumer names (Tencent, Xiaomi) over pure-semi exposure. Watch whether the AI-capex-peak narrative deepens or fades; it is the main new risk against the otherwise-supportive China-stimulus backdrop.

items.headline: Silver holds ~$58.9 and oil eases as the Iran pause takes the edge off the rate-hike trade
items.summary: Silver reclaimed and held roughly $58.4-58.9/oz over the weekend (JM Bullion live ~$58.88 on Sat 26 Jul), after returning above $58 on Friday (+~2% on the day) — the sub-$58 break from Thursday did not stick. Gold sat ~$4,050-4,057. Oil, the channel that had forced the hawkish Fed repricing, eased into the weekend (Brent Fri close ~$96.8), and with US-Iran strikes paused the 27 Jul futures reopen skews lower rather than higher.
items.actionable: The levered silver core is the portfolio's biggest short-term swing factor and it held the $58 line through the stress — a constructive tell. If the Iran pause holds and oil reopens lower, the rate-hike fear that pressures silver 2-3x more than gold should ease further; treat $57-58 as the line and the 29 Jul FOMC as the next binary. Gold-heavy GDX remains the steadier way to hold metals exposure.

items.headline: FOMC 28-29 Jul preview: hawkish-hold base case, but ~38% now price a 25bp HIKE
items.summary: The Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh since May 2026) is widely expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on 28-29 Jul, but the mid-week oil spike pushed CME FedWatch hike odds to ~38% (from ~11% on 15 Jul), with September hike odds above 80%. No surveyed economist expects a hike; Citi frames the move as a 'risk premium' tied to Warsh's no-forward-guidance regime and rising oil. June CPI cooled to 3.5% headline / 2.6% core, but energy keeps the Fed cautious. Decision Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET; no SEP at this meeting. Q2 GDP and PCE also land this week.
items.actionable: A live ~1-in-3 hike is the core near-term threat to levered silver and SGX REITs, keeping rates higher-for-longer. But the weekend Iran de-escalation eases the oil impulse behind those odds — the big USD cash pile (earning ~3.5-3.75%) stays productive dry powder; let the 29 Jul print and the oil reopen resolve before redeploying into rate-sensitive names. A dovish Warsh surprise is the upside catalyst.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds ~$64k, Ether ~$1,860, crypto Fear&Greed recovers to 37 into the weekend
items.summary: Bitcoin held above $64,000 into the weekend (opened ~$65,048 Fri, watching the $64k support), with Ether around $1,855-1,877 and the crypto Fear&Greed index recovering to ~37 (Fear) from ~27. Prices had retreated Thursday-Friday on higher Treasury yields, tariff-driven inflation expectations and a ~$225M single-day spot-BTC-ETF outflow that broke a week-long inflow streak. No crypto-specific bullish driver — the market is trading as a pure risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto moves in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade — the same Iran-pause risk-relief that would help silver is a mild tailwind here, hence the sentiment recovery to 37. Treat it as a barometer; the EU's new offshore-crypto sanctions remain a structural overhang keeping crypto exposure modest versus the metals core.

items.headline: China's 24 Jul Politburo signals stronger-than-expected H2 stimulus; anti-'involution' pricing-law draft
items.summary: The 24-member Politburo, chaired by Xi, met on H2 economic work and issued stronger-than-expected wording — pledging countercyclical policy 'with precision and force.' The same day the NDRC and market regulator released a draft amendment to China's pricing law (its first update since 1998) targeting 'disorderly low-price competition' (anti-involution). The signalling lands after Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3%, the weakest in three-plus years.
items.actionable: The binary the book was waiting on resolved to the upside — the Politburo's forceful language and the anti-involution pricing reform support the HK-tech core (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) into earnings, and the divergence Friday (internet names up, chips down on the AI-capex scare) argues for favoring Tencent/Xiaomi over the semi leg. Watch for follow-through detail at the late-Jul/Aug policy meetings before adding.

items.headline: Gold holds ~$4,055 below a $4,130 two-week high as safe-haven demand fights rate crosscurrents
items.summary: Gold hit a two-week high near $4,130 on 22 July on Iran-war safe-haven bids and a softer dollar, then eased to ~$4,050-4,057 by 24 July as oil-driven inflation fears and higher yields (10Y ~4.69%) capped it. Dip-buying persisted near $4,050 and gold funds drew ~+$2.0bn in the latest weekly flows, though BofA continues to flag a gold 'death cross' and elevated net-longs into the Fed.
items.actionable: Gold is holding up far better than silver in this regime — favor the gold-heavy miners (GDX) over pure silver leverage while the war/inflation tug-of-war persists. The ~$4,130 high is the level to reclaim; a hawkish Fed could fade it toward $4,000, while a durable Iran de-escalation that relieves rates would support both metals.

items.headline: Singapore banks at record highs as earnings open; DBS guides FY2026 profit slightly lower
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB hit fresh record highs in July (DBS above S$70) on wealth-management fee income cushioning lower rates, ahead of DBS's 6 Aug results. SGX reporting season opened 23 Jul after hours — Mapletree Industrial Trust posted a DPU of 3.11 cents (-4.9% y/y), and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug. DBS has guided FY2026 net profit slightly below 2025 while reaffirming its 15-cent/quarter capital-return dividend.
items.actionable: SGX banks ride record highs into 6 Aug DBS earnings — supportive for the blue-chip sleeve, but record valuations meet softening guidance and REIT DPUs (Mapletree Industrial -4.9%) already reflect the rate drag. If the Iran pause holds and rates ease, the REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT) get relief; watch the yield backdrop and the end-July MAS review.

items.headline: MAS reported to be imposing a single S-REIT leverage limit and added disclosures (pending confirmation)
items.summary: Singapore market coverage reports MAS is moving to a single aggregate-leverage limit and additional disclosure requirements for all SGX-listed REITs. The exact effective date and the numeric gearing cap were not confirmable from secondary sources this run and should be verified against the MAS primary release before acting. It would directly touch the portfolio's S-REIT sleeve.
items.actionable: A single leverage cap is a double-edged change for the S-REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT, CapLand China Trust) — clearer rules and more disclosure vs a potential constraint on gearing/acquisitions. Flagged as reported-but-unconfirmed: confirm the cap and date on the MAS site before repositioning the REIT sleeve.

items.headline: Houthi blockade forces Saudi crude tankers to U-turn; Saudi Arabia strikes Houthis in Yemen
items.summary: At least seven Saudi crude tankers reversed course toward Suez after the Houthis emailed shipowners warning against calling at Saudi ports; the broader 2026 Hormuz/Red Sea crisis has damaged ~17 merchant ships. Saudi Arabia said it launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen after another Saudi vessel was attacked, widening the conflict beyond the direct US-Iran axis and adding a second front to the shipping/energy disruption.
items.actionable: The Red Sea/Yemen front is the residual escalation risk even with the direct US-Iran strikes paused — it keeps a floor under oil and a bid under gold if the maritime disruption widens again. Reinforces gold-heavy GDX and the energy sleeve as a hedge against the Iran pause breaking down.

items.headline: Tencent fires manager over leaked pay; Xiaomi's on-device MiMo LLM cleared; SMIC sees southbound selling
items.summary: Tencent fired a manager whose seven-figure compensation package leaked and went viral on Chinese social media (24 Jul). In flows, Tencent drew southbound net buying (~HK$2.3bn) while SMIC saw net selling (~HK$1.08bn); Xiaomi's self-developed on-device MiMo model passed China's national LLM registry filing — an AI-positive catalyst for the phone/EV maker.
items.actionable: Idiosyncratic single-stock noise inside the HK-tech core: Tencent's headline is cosmetic and its southbound buying is the better tell; Xiaomi's model approval is a genuine AI catalyst; SMIC's net selling compounds the Friday AI-overcapacity hit. Nets to holding Tencent as the core with Xiaomi as the higher-beta AI catch-up and SMIC as the most exposed leg.

items.headline: Trump EO bars defense contractors from adversary-sourced critical materials — rare-earth reshoring tailwind
items.summary: Trump signed an executive order (20 Jul) further barring US defense contractors from sourcing critical materials from adversaries and directing the Pentagon to mitigate supply-chain national-security risks. It reinforces the structural US rare-earth reshoring push that already includes the DoD's ~15% MP Materials stake, a $110/kg NdPr price floor and a 10-year magnet offtake, plus ~$1.2bn of OSC loans (Energy Fuels, Phoenix Tailings) in June.
items.actionable: Another layer of Western government demand under the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — bullish MP and government-backed UUUU most directly. But with China's export controls suspended to 10 Nov (magnet exports +75% MoM), near-term pricing urgency is eased: accumulate on weakness into the control-snap-back catalyst rather than chase.

items.headline: EU adopts 21st Russia sanctions package — largest in 4 years, targets crypto rails
items.summary: The EU Council adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package — 218 listings, the largest batch in four years — targeting energy, banks, the shadow fleet and crypto. It bans transactions with 14 offshore crypto platforms and creates authority to blanket-ban crypto services from entire third countries facilitating sanctions evasion. Rubio and Lavrov met on the ASEAN sidelines in Manila on 23 July, keeping a diplomatic channel open.
items.actionable: A structural tightening of offshore crypto rails adds regulatory overhang to the crypto sleeve — a reason to keep crypto exposure modest versus the metals core; low direct relevance to the portfolio beyond that.
